I must not implement it, and say so in AGENTS.md.

Mod update check via Modrinth API: client-side, on-demand. Need to know installed mods: Fabric `FabricLoader.getInstance().getAllMods()` includes mods with `getMetadata().getVersion().getFriendlyString()` and id; NeoForge `ModList.get().getMods()` with `ModInfo.getModId()`, version, and `IModInfo.getModURL()`/`getOwningFile().getFile().getModId()`. Map to Modrinth via `GET https://api.modrinth.com/v2/project/{id}/version?loaders=[...]&game_versions=[...]` — but mapping modid→modrinth slug needs a lookup: `POST https://api.modrinth.com/v2/version_file_lookup` requires sha1 hashes of jars. Actually the correct Modrinth approach: use the jar's SHA-1/SHA-512 with `POST /v2/version_files` (bulk: `POST /v2/version_files` with hashes + algorithm). That's the proper way and policy-friendly. Getting the jar path: `FabricLoader...getModContainer().getOrigin().getPaths()`; NeoForge: `ModList.get().getModFileById(id).getFile().getFilePath()`. Then compute sha1 and query `POST https://api.modrinth.com/v2/version_files` with `{"hashes":[...],"algorithm":"sha1"}` → returns versions. Then `POST /v2/version_files/update` with `{"hashes":[...],"algorithm":"sha1","loaders":["fabric"],"game_versions":["1.21.8"]}` → gives latest matching version. That is exactly the documented endpoint.

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * One thing that can be scanned and cleaned.
 *
 * @param id       stable identifier, also the suffix of the {@code cleanmcmod.target.<id>} lang key
 * @param category where the target comes from
 * @param safety   whether deleting it forces a re-download
 * @param path     absolute, normalised path inside the game directory
 * @param label    literal display name for detected/custom targets, or {@code null} for built-ins
 */
public record CacheTarget(String id, CacheCategory category, CacheSafety safety, Path path, String label) {

    public CacheTarget {
        Objects.requireNonNull(id, "id");
        Objects.requireNonNull(category, "category");
        Objects.requireNonNull(safety, "safety");
        Objects.requireNonNull(path, "path");
        path = path.toAbsolutePath().normalize();
    }

    public static CacheTarget builtin(String id, CacheCategory category, CacheSafety safety, Path path) {
        return new CacheTarget(id, category, safety, path, null);
    }

    public static CacheTarget detected(String id, CacheCategory category, CacheSafety safety, Path path, String label) {
        return new CacheTarget(id, category, safety, path, label);
    }

    public String translationKey() {
        return "cleanmcmod.target." + id;
    }

    /** Path relative to {@code gameDir}, with forward slashes, for logs and labels. */
    public String relativePath(Path gameDir) {
        Path root = gameDir.toAbsolutePath().normalize();
        Path rel = path.startsWith(root) ? root.relativize(path) : path;
        String text = rel.toString().replace('\\', '/');
        return text.isEmpty() ? "." : text;
    }
}

public record CacheScan(List<TargetState> targets, int files, long bytes) {

    public CacheScan {
        targets = List.copyOf(targets);
    }

        int files = 0;
        long bytes = 0L;
        for (TargetState state : targets) {

            bytes += state.bytes();

        return presentTargets().size();
    }

    public boolean empty() {
        return presentCount() == 0;

{"kind":"tool","id":"csxCMyS2TaY","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/CacheScanner.java","instructions":"Read-only cache measurement.","content":"package de.piboh.cleanmcmod.clean;

import de.piboh.cleanmcmod.CleanMcMod;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.FileVisitResult;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.LinkOption;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.SimpleFileVisitor;
import java.nio.file.attribute.BasicFileAttributes;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/** Measures cache targets without touching them. */
public final class CacheScanner {

    public TargetState scan(CacheTarget target) {
        Path path = target.path();
        if (!Files.exists(path, LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS)) {
            return TargetState.missing(target);
        }
        Counter counter = new Counter();
        try {
            Files.walkFileTree(path, counter);
        } catch (IOException e) {
            CleanMcMod.LOGGER.warn("Could not measure {}: {}", path, e.toString());
        }
        return new TargetState(target, true, counter.files, counter.bytes);
    }

    public CacheScan scanAll(List<CacheTarget> targets) {
        List<TargetState> states = new ArrayList<>(targets.size());
        for (CacheTarget target : targets) {
            states.add(scan(target));
        }
        return CacheScan.of(states);
    }

    /** Counts regular files and their size. Symbolic links are counted but never followed. */
    private static final class Counter extends SimpleFileVisitor<Path> {
        private int files;
        private long bytes;

        @Override
        public FileVisitResult visitFile(Path file, BasicFileAttributes attrs) {
            files++;
            if (attrs.isRegularFile()) {
                bytes += attrs.size();
            }
            return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
        }

        @Override
        public FileVisitResult visitFileFailed(Path file, IOException exc) {
            return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
        }
    }
}

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

/** Outcome of a clean run: one entry per target plus aggregate totals. */
public record CleanReport(boolean dryRun, long durationMillis, List<TargetResult> results) {

    public CleanReport {
        results = List.copyOf(results);
    }

    public int filesDeleted() {
        int total = 0;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.filesDeleted();
        }
        return total;
    }

    public long bytesFreed() {
        long total = 0L;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.bytesFreed();
        }
        return total;
    }

    public long cleanedTargets() {
        return results.stream().filter(TargetResult::successful).count();
    }

    /** Human readable volume, e.g. {@code 1.4 MiB}. */
    public static String formatBytes(long bytes) {
        if (bytes < 1024L) {
            return bytes + " B";
        }
        double value = bytes;
        String[] units = {"KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"};
        int unit = -1;
        do {
            value /= 1024.0;
            unit++;
        } while (value >= 1024.0 && unit < units.length - 1);
        return String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.1f %s", value, units[unit]);
    }

    public String summary() {
        return "%s%d targets, %d files, %s".formatted(
                dryRun ? "[dry run] " : "", cleanedTargets(), filesDeleted(), formatBytes(bytesFreed()));
    }
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"csxO3B6ZhBE","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/TargetResult.java","instructions":"Result of cleaning one target.","content":"package de.piboh.cleanmcmod.clean;

/** What happened to a single cache target during a clean run. */
public record TargetResult(
        String targetId,
        TargetStatus status,
        int filesDeleted,
        long bytesFreed,
        int filesSkipped,
        String message) {

    public static final String NOT_PRESENT = "not present";

    public TargetResult {
        filesDeleted = Math.max(0, filesDeleted);
        bytesFreed = Math.max(0L, bytesFreed);
        filesSkipped = Math.max(0, filesSkipped);
    }

    public boolean successful() {
        return status == TargetStatus.CLEANED || status == TargetStatus.PARTIAL || status == TargetStatus.DRY_RUN;
    }

    /** One log/CLI line, English only — in-game text is built from the lang files. */
    public String describe() {
        return switch (status) {
            case CLEANED -> "%s: %d files, %s".formatted(targetId, filesDeleted, CleanReport.formatBytes(bytesFreed));
            case PARTIAL -> "%s: %d files, %s (%d skipped: %s)".formatted(
                    targetId, filesDeleted, CleanReport.formatBytes(bytesFreed), filesSkipped, message);
            case DRY_RUN -> "%s: would delete %d files, %s".formatted(
                    targetId, filesDeleted, CleanReport.formatBytes(bytesFreed));
            case MISSING -> targetId + ": " + NOT_PRESENT;
            case FAILED -> "%s: failed (%s)".formatted(targetId, message);
        };
    }
}

/**

 *
 * <p>The defaults only touch caches the game regenerates by itself. Anything that forces a
 * re-download is off until the user asks for it.</p>
 */
public final class CleanMcModConfig {

    private static final Gson GSON = new GsonBuilder().setPrettyPrinting().create();

    public boolean includeLogs = true;
    public boolean includeCrashReports = true;
    public boolean includeDebugDumps = true;
    public boolean includeServerResourcePacks = true;
    public boolean includeLoaderCaches = true;
    public boolean includeAssetCache = false;
    public boolean autoDetect = true;
    public boolean dryRun = false;
    public List<String> extraPaths = new ArrayList<>();

    public List<String> extraPaths() {
        return extraPaths == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(extraPaths);
    }

    public static CleanMcModConfig load(Path file) {
        if (!Files.isRegularFile(file)) {
            return new CleanMcModConfig();
        }
        try (Reader reader = Files.newBufferedReader(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            CleanMcModConfig config = GSON.fromJson(reader, CleanMcModConfig.class);
            return config == null ? new CleanMcModConfig() : config;
        } catch (IOException | JsonParseException e) {
            CleanMcMod.LOGGER.warn("Could not read config {}: {}", file, e.toString());
            return new CleanMcModConfig();
        }
    }

    public static void save(CleanMcModConfig config, Path file) {
        try {
            Path parent = file.getParent();
            if (parent != null) {
                Files.createDirectories(parent);
            }
            try (Writer writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
                GSON.toJson(config, writer);
            }
        } catch (IOException e) {
            CleanMcMod.LOGGER.warn("Could not write config {}: {}", file, e.toString());
        }
    }
}

        List<TargetState> present = current.presentTargets();

        int left = this.width / 2 - 156;

            Text name = Texts.targetName(state.target());
            String measured = "%d · %s".formatted(state.files(), CleanReport.formatBytes(state.bytes()));
            int measuredWidth = this.textRenderer.getWidth(measured);

            context.drawText(this.textRenderer, name, left, y, color, false);
            context.drawText(this.textRenderer, Text.literal(measured), right - measuredWidth, y, Texts.COLOR_INFO, false);

            if (result != null) {
                Text statusLine = Texts.status(result);
                int statusWidth = this.textRenderer.getWidth(statusLine);
                context.drawText(this.textRenderer, statusLine, right - measuredWidth - statusWidth - 8, y,
                        Texts.statusColor(result), false);
            }
            y += 11;
        }

        int hidden = present.size() - maxRows;
        if (hidden > 0) {
            context.drawText(this.textRenderer, Text.translatable("cleanmcmod.screen.main.more", hidden),
                    left, y, Texts.COLOR_INFO, false);
        }
    }

    private TargetResult findResult(TargetState state) {
        if (shownReport == null) {
            return null;
        }
        for (TargetResult result : shownReport.results()) {
            if (result.targetId().equals(state.target().id())) {
                return result;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean shouldPause() {
        return false;
    }
}

```java
    public List<CacheTarget> detect(Path gameDir) {
        Path root = gameDir.toAbsolutePath().normalize();
        if (!Files.isDirectory(root)) {
            return List.of();
        }
        List<CacheTarget> found = new ArrayList<>();
        try {
            Files.walkFileTree(root, EnumSet.noneOf(FileVisitOption.class), Integer.MAX_VALUE, new SimpleFileVisitor<>() {
                @Override
                public FileVisitResult preVisitDirectory(Path dir, BasicFileAttributes attrs) {
                    if (dir.equals(root)) {
                        return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                    }
                    if (found.size() >= MAX_TARGETS) {
                        return FileVisitResult.TERMINATE;
                    }
                    Path relative = root.relativize(dir);
                    if (isExcluded(relative)) {
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    if (CACHE_DIR_NAMES.contains(name(dir))) {
                        found.add(detected(root, dir, relative, "cache folder"));
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    // config/ is small and is where mods nest their caches; elsewhere stop early.
                    if (!isUnderConfig(relative) && relative.getNameCount() >= MAX_DEPTH) {
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                }

                @Override
                public FileVisitResult visitFile(Path file, BasicFileAttributes attrs) {
                    // With an unbounded walk every directory arrives through preVisitDirectory, so a
                    // directory can never be mistaken for a cache file here.
                    if (!attrs.isRegularFile() || found.size() >= MAX_TARGETS) {
                        return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                    }
                    Path relative = root.relativize(file);
                    if (isExcluded(relative)) return CONTINUE;
                    if (name(file).endsWith(".cache")) found.add(...);
                    return CONTINUE;
                }
                ...
            });
        } catch (IOException e) { ... }
        return List.copyOf(found);
    }
```

import java.util.Objects;

/** What happened to a single cache target during a clean run. */
public record TargetResult(
        String targetId,
        TargetStatus status,
        Counts deleted,
        Counts planned,
        int filesSkipped,
        String message) {

    public static final String NOT_PRESENT = "not present";

    public TargetResult {
        Objects.requireNonNull(targetId, "targetId");
        Objects.requireNonNull(status, "status");
        Objects.requireNonNull(deleted, "deleted");
        Objects.requireNonNull(planned, "planned");
        filesSkipped = Math.max(0, filesSkipped);
    }

    /**
     * A file/volume pair. {@code deleted} is what actually left the disk; {@code planned} is what a
     * dry run would remove. Exactly one of them is non-zero, and a dry run always reports
     * {@link #filesDeleted()} as zero.
     */
    public record Counts(int files, long bytes) {
        public static final Counts NONE = new Counts(0, 0L);

        public Counts {
            files = Math.max(0, files);
            bytes = Math.max(0L, bytes);
        }
    }

    public static TargetResult missing(String targetId) {
        return new TargetResult(targetId, TargetStatus.MISSING, Counts.NONE, Counts.NONE, 0, NOT_PRESENT);
    }

    public static TargetResult failed(String targetId, String message) {
        return new TargetResult(targetId, TargetStatus.FAILED, Counts.NONE, Counts.NONE, 0, message);
    }

    public static TargetResult wouldRemove(String targetId, int files, long bytes) {
        return new TargetResult(targetId, TargetStatus.DRY_RUN, Counts.NONE, new Counts(files, bytes), 0, null);
    }

    public static TargetResult removed(String targetId, int files, long bytes, int filesSkipped, String message) {
        TargetStatus status = filesSkipped > 0 ? TargetStatus.PARTIAL : TargetStatus.CLEANED;
        return new TargetResult(targetId, status, new Counts(files, bytes), Counts.NONE, filesSkipped, message);
    }

    public boolean successful() {
        return status == TargetStatus.CLEANED || status == TargetStatus.PARTIAL || status == TargetStatus.DRY_RUN;
    }

    /** One log/CLI line, English only — in-game text is built from the lang files. */
    public String describe() {
        return switch (status) {
            case CLEANED -> "%s: %d files, %s".formatted(
                    targetId, deleted.files(), CleanReport.formatBytes(deleted.bytes()));
            case PARTIAL -> "%s: %d files, %s (%d skipped: %s)".formatted(
                    targetId, deleted.files(), CleanReport.formatBytes(deleted.bytes()), filesSkipped, message);
            case DRY_RUN -> "%s: would delete %d files, %s".formatted(
                    targetId, planned.files(), CleanReport.formatBytes(planned.bytes()));
            case MISSING -> targetId + ": " + NOT_PRESENT;
            case FAILED -> "%s: failed (%s)".formatted(targetId, message);
        };
    }
}

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;

/** Outcome of a clean run: one entry per target plus aggregate totals. */
public record CleanReport(boolean dryRun, long durationMillis, List<TargetResult> results) {

    public CleanReport {
        results = List.copyOf(results);
    }

    /** Files actually removed. Always zero for a dry run. */
    public int filesDeleted() {
        int total = 0;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.deleted().files();
        }
        return total;
    }

    /** Bytes actually freed. Always zero for a dry run. */
    public long bytesFreed() {
        long total = 0L;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.deleted().bytes();
        }
        return total;
    }

    /** Files a dry run would remove; zero when the run deleted for real. */
    public int filesPlanned() {
        int total = 0;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.planned().files();
        }
        return total;
    }

    /** Bytes a dry run would free; zero when the run deleted for real. */
    public long bytesPlanned() {
        long total = 0L;
        for (TargetResult result : results) {
            total += result.planned().bytes();
        }
        return total;
    }

    /** Targets that existed and were cleaned, or that a dry run would clean. */
    public long cleanedTargets() {
        return results.stream().filter(TargetResult::successful).count();
    }

    /** Human readable volume, e.g. {@code 1.4 MiB}. */
    public static String formatBytes(long bytes) {
        if (bytes < 1024L) {
            return bytes + " B";
        }
        double value = bytes;
        String[] units = {"KiB", "MiB", "GiB", "TiB"};
        int unit = -1;
        do {
            value /= 1024.0;
            unit++;
        } while (value >= 1024.0 && unit < units.length - 1);
        return String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.1f %s", value, units[unit]);
    }

    public String summary() {
        if (dryRun) {
            return "[dry run] %d targets, %d files would be removed, %s would be freed".formatted(
                    cleanedTargets(), filesPlanned(), formatBytes(bytesPlanned()));
        }
        return "%d targets, %d files, %s".formatted(cleanedTargets(), filesDeleted(), formatBytes(bytesFreed()));
    }
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"cuTYs9lyQBE","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/CacheAutoDetector.java","instructions":"Fix traversal so directories are never seen as files; walk config to any depth.","content":"package de.piboh.cleanmcmod.clean;

import de.piboh.cleanmcmod.CleanMcMod;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.FileVisitResult;
import java.nio.file.FileVisitOption;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.SimpleFileVisitor;
import java.nio.file.attribute.BasicFileAttributes;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.EnumSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Finds caches that mods create without registering them anywhere.
 *
 * <p>Mods are free to write wherever they like, so the only portable rule is "a folder called
 * cache/caches/.cache, or a file ending in .cache, is a cache". User data folders are excluded,
 * because a mod's save data must never be deleted by a cache cleaner. Installed resource packs and
 * shader packs are excluded as well: they are user content, not caches.</p>
 *
 * <p>The walk is unbounded and prunes itself: directories are therefore always delivered to
 * {@link SimpleFileVisitor#preVisitDirectory}, never to {@code visitFile} as a "file" of unknown
 * type. That distinction used to hide the most common layout, {@code config/<mod>/cache}. Outside
 * {@code config/} the walk stops at {@link #MAX_DEPTH} levels, which keeps a full game directory
 * cheap to scan; {@code config/} is small and is walked to any depth, because that is where mods
 * nest their caches.</p>
 */
public final class CacheAutoDetector {

    private static final Set<String> CACHE_DIR_NAMES = Set.of("cache", "caches", ".cache");
    private static final Set<String> EXCLUDED_DIRS = Set.of(
            "saves", "resourcepacks", "shaderpacks", "mods", "libraries", "versions",
            "assets", "screenshots", "backups", ".git", ".freebuff", ".ignore");
    private static final String CONFIG_DIR = "config";
    private static final int MAX_DEPTH = 4;
    private static final int MAX_TARGETS = 24;

    public List<CacheTarget> detect(Path gameDir) {
        Path root = gameDir.toAbsolutePath().normalize();
        if (!Files.isDirectory(root)) {
            return List.of();
        }
        List<CacheTarget> found = new ArrayList<>();
        try {
            Files.walkFileTree(root, EnumSet.noneOf(FileVisitOption.class), Integer.MAX_VALUE, new SimpleFileVisitor<>() {
                @Override
                public FileVisitResult preVisitDirectory(Path dir, BasicFileAttributes attrs) {
                    if (dir.equals(root)) {
                        return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                    }
                    if (found.size() >= MAX_TARGETS) {
                        return FileVisitResult.TERMINATE;
                    }
                    Path relative = root.relativize(dir);
                    if (isExcluded(relative)) {
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    if (CACHE_DIR_NAMES.contains(name(dir))) {
                        found.add(detected(root, dir, relative, "cache folder"));
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    if (!isUnderConfig(relative) && relative.getNameCount() >= MAX_DEPTH) {
                        return FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
                    }
                    return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                }

                @Override
                public FileVisitResult visitFile(Path file, BasicFileAttributes attrs) {
                    if (!attrs.isRegularFile() || found.size() >= MAX_TARGETS) {
                        return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                    }
                    Path relative = root.relativize(file);
                    if (isExcluded(relative)) {
                        return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                    }
                    if (name(file).endsWith(".cache")) {
                        found.add(detected(root, file, relative, "cache file"));
                    }
                    return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                }

                @Override
                public FileVisitResult visitFileFailed(Path file, IOException exc) {
                    return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
                }
            });
        } catch (IOException e) {
            CleanMcMod.LOGGER.debug("Cache auto-detection stopped early: {}", e.toString());
        }
        return List.copyOf(found);
    }

    private static CacheTarget detected(Path root, Path path, Path relative, String kind) {
        return CacheTarget.detected(
                idFor(relative),
                CacheCategory.MOD,
                CacheSafety.SAFE,
                path,
                kind + ": " + relative.toString().replace('\\', '/'));
    }

    private static String name(Path path) {
        return path.getFileName().toString().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
    }

    private static boolean isUnderConfig(Path relative) {
        Path first = relative.getName(0);
        return first != null && CONFIG_DIR.equalsIgnoreCase(first.toString());
    }

    private static boolean isExcluded(Path relative) {
        for (Path part : relative) {
            if (EXCLUDED_DIRS.contains(part.toString().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT))) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

    static String idFor(Path relative) {
        String text = relative.toString().replace('\\', '/').toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        return "detected_" + text.replaceAll("[^a-z0-9]+", "_");
    }
}

## I due difetti sono chiusi

**1. `CacheAutoDetector` — semantica del walk, non il numero di profondità** ([CacheAutoDetector.java](src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/CacheAutoDetector.java))

La causa vera era quella che l'audit aveva isolato: con un `maxDepth` finito la directory al limite arriva a `visitFile` e viene scartata come "non un file regolare". Ora il walk è **unbounded** (`Integer.MAX_VALUE`) e si pota da solo:

- `preVisitDirectory` è l'unico posto in cui nascono target-directory, quindi **una directory non può più essere scambiata per un file, a nessuna profondità**;
- `config/` viene percorsa a qualsiasi profondità (è lì che i mod annidano le cache); fuori da `config/` il taglio a 4 livelli resta, perché scansionare `journeymap/` o `saves/` profondi non serve e costerebbe;
- restano escluse le cartelle di dati utente (`saves`, `resourcepacks`, `shaderpacks`, `mods`, `assets`, …) e resta il `SKIP_SUBTREE` su una cache trovata, così non si duplicano target annidati.

**2. Dry run: "pianificato" separato da "fatto"** ([TargetResult.java](src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/TargetResult.java), [CleanReport.java](src/main/java/de/piboh/cleanmcmod/clean/CleanReport.java))

`TargetResult` ora porta due coppie distinte — `deleted` e `planned` (`Counts(files, bytes)`) — con factory `cleaned/partial/wouldRemove/missing/failed`. Di conseguenza `CleanReport.filesDeleted()`/`bytesFreed()` sono **davvero 0 in dry run**, mentre `filesPlanned()`/`bytesPlanned()` raccontano cosa verrebbe rimosso. Il comando usa la coppia giusta e ha una riga dedicata ([`cleanmcmod.command.clean.done_dry`](src/main/resources/assets/cleanmcmod/lang/en_us.json)) invece di stampare "freed" per file mai toccati.

plugins {
    id 'fabric-loom' version "${loom_version}"
    id 'java'
}

// version.txt is the single source of truth for the mod version.
def modVersion = rootProject.file('version.txt').text.trim()
version = "${modVersion}+${minecraft_version}"
group = 'piboh.cleanmc.mod'

base {
    archivesName = 'cleanmcmod'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    minecraft "com.mojang:minecraft:${minecraft_version}"
    mappings "net.fabricmc:yarn:${yarn_mappings}:v2"
    modImplementation "net.fabricmc:fabric-loader:${loader_version}"
    modImplementation "net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api:${fabric_api_version}"

    testImplementation platform('org.junit:junit-bom:5.11.4')
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter'
    testImplementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.11.0'
    testRuntimeOnly 'org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher'
}

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(java_version as int)
    }
    withSourcesJar()
}

tasks.withType(JavaCompile).configureEach {
    options.encoding = 'UTF-8'
    options.release = java_version as int
}

processResources {
    inputs.property 'version', modVersion
    inputs.property 'minecraft_dep', minecraft_dep
    filesMatching('fabric.mod.json') {
        expand version: modVersion, minecraft_dep: minecraft_dep
    }
}

tasks.named('test') {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    testLogging {
        events 'passed', 'failed', 'skipped'
    }
}

jar {
    from(rootProject.file('LICENSE')) {
        rename { "${it}_cleanmcmod" }
    }
}

using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public class W {
 [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool GetClientRect(IntPtr h, out RECT r);
 [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool ClientToScreen(IntPtr h, ref POINT p);

$hh = $rect.B - $rect.T

    [W]::mouse_event(0x0002, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 120
    [W]::mouse_event(0x0004, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)
    Write-Output "clicked gui=$x,$y px=$($x*$scale),$($y*$scale)"
  }
  "scroll" {
    [void][W]::SetForegroundWindow($h)
    [void][W]::SetCursorPos($origin.X + ($x * $scale), $origin.Y + ($y * $scale))

    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    [System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait($text)
    Write-Output "keys=$text"
  }
}

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Project overview

**VIVI Music** is an open-source (GPL-3.0) Android client for YouTube Music /
YouTube (ad-free streaming, Apple Music–style UI), plus its companion **desktop
edition** ("VIVI Music DE", Compose Multiplatform) and a cross-device
**sync** layer that keeps the two in sync. It is a fork of the
ViMusic/InnerTune/SimpMusic family.

- **Language/build**: Kotlin 2.x, Java 21 toolchain, Gradle Kotlin DSL.
- **Android app**: Jetpack Compose + Material 3, Hilt, Room, DataStore,
  Media3/ExoPlayer.
- **Desktop app**: Compose Multiplatform (native Windows / Linux / macOS).
- **Shared network layer**: pure-JVM Kotlin modules reused by both Android and
  desktop.

## 2. Architecture and module structure

`settings.gradle.kts` declares `rootProject.name = "vivimusic"` and these modules:

| Module | Type | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `app` | Android (`com.android.application`) | Main app: UI, playback, DB, viewmodels, services, widgets |
| `innertube` | Kotlin JVM | YouTube Music inner-API client (search/browse/next/player, signature decipher) |
| `spotify` | Kotlin JVM | Spotify auth + playlist import |
| `lastfm` | Kotlin JVM | Last.fm scrobbling |
| `kizzy` | Kotlin JVM | Discord Rich Presence (WebSocket gateway) |
| `shazamkit` | Kotlin JVM | Shazam-style song recognition |
| `jiosaavn` | Kotlin JVM | JioSaavn streaming provider (CDN link decryption) |
| `lyricsProvider` | Kotlin JVM | Lyrics providers (KuGou, LrcLib, Musixmatch, PaxSenix, …) + the shared lyric model/parser/romanizer (`com.music.lyrics`, JVM port of the mobile `LyricsUtils`) |
| `sync` | Kotlin JVM | Cross-device sync: data model + WebSocket client (pairing, push/pull) |
| `desktop` | Kotlin JVM + Compose Multiplatform | Desktop app (reuses the JVM modules above) |
| `canvas`, `artistvideo`, `applecanvas`, `vivimusiccanvas` | Android | Animated canvases / visualizers |
| `sync-server` | Node.js (not a Gradle module) | WebSocket relay for Android↔Desktop pairing + mailbox |

Key paths:

- `app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/` — app code (see `ui/`, `playback/`,
  `viewmodels/`, `db/`, `constants/`, `di/`, `utils/`, `devicesync/`,
  `listentogether/`).
- `app/src/main/res/values*/strings.xml` — Android string resources
  (localization, see §6).
- `app/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/constants/PreferenceKeys.kt` — all
  DataStore preference keys + `LanguageCodeToName` map.
- `desktop/src/main/kotlin/com/music/vivi/desktop/` — desktop entry point and UI.
- `.github/workflows/` — CI (per-OS desktop builds + auto-release).

The `innertube`, `spotify`, `lastfm`, `kizzy`, `shazamkit`, `lyricsProvider`,
`jiosaavn`, and `sync` modules are **pure JVM**: do not introduce Android
dependencies there, or you break the desktop build.

## 3. Code conventions and development guidelines

- **Branch policy (mandatory) — three roles, never mix them**:
  - `vivi-music-de` — home of the desktop edition AND of the mobile code used to
    build the APK for the DE release. **DE-only** changes are committed and
    pushed **only** here.

Instructions for AI coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Project overview

**CleanMCMod** is a **client-only** Minecraft mod that clears the caches which
make the game render wrong: stale `logs/`, crash reports, debug dumps, the
server resource-pack cache, Fabric's remapped-jar cache, Mixin debug output and
the asset cache, plus the per-mod cache folders that mods create under
`config/<mod>/`. It also lists the mods installed in `mods/` and, on request,
installs newer versions from the Modrinth API.

- **Language/build**: Java 21 source/target, Gradle (Fabric Loom 1.19.3).
- **Loader**: Fabric Loader. The jar is built against `piboh.cleanmc.mod` and
  declares `environment: client` — it never runs on a dedicated server.
- **Targets**: Minecraft 1.21.8 – 1.21.11 (Java 21) and 26.1 / 26.2 / 26.3
  (Java 25). The Minecraft version is a build dimension
  (`gradle.properties`), not a branch of code.
- **Version**: `version.txt` at the repo root is the single source of truth.
  `build.gradle` reads it; `fabric.mod.json` is expanded from it. Never
  hard-code a version in Java or in the JSON.

## 2. Architecture and package structure

Root package `piboh.cleanmc.mod`, four concerns, one owner of state each:

| Package | Files | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `clean` | `CacheTargets`, `CacheTarget`, `CacheCategory`, `CacheSafety`, `CacheScanner [… 6,793 characters omitted] ed(glob.glob("src/main/resources/assets/cleanmcmod/lang/*.json")):

      assert set(d) == set(base), f"{p}: key drift"
      for k in base:

## 7. Versioning

- `version.txt` holds `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. `build.gradle` builds

  version come from it.
- Bump `version.txt` only when the released artifact changes meaning. Never

## 8. Modrinth / CurseForge policy — mandatory

- The mod is **client-side only** and must stay that way (`environment:

- API use is polite: no polling loops, no background scheduler, no telemetry.

## 9. What is not implemented (do not claim otherwise)

- No mod hiding, no anti-cheat evasion, no server resource-pack bypass.

path, why, and whether the game regenerates it. Wrong deletions are not

A client-side Minecraft mod that clears the caches that make the game glitch —
broken GUIs, purple-and-black missing models, stale resource packs — and that
updates your installed mods from Modrinth when you ask it to.

No world edits, no server side, no background tasks. It only touches cache
folders and, if you confirm it, the jars in `mods/`.

## What it cleans

| Target | Why it exists |
|---|---|
| `logs/` | Game logs. Rewritten on every launch. |
| `crash-reports/` | Crash reports. Created only when something fails. |
| `debug/` | Debug dumps left by the game. |
| `server-resource-packs/` | Server packs cached by the game. |
| Fabric remapped-jar cache | `fabric-remapped-*` jars rebuilt from `mods/`. |
| Mixin debug output | Only present when Mixin debugging was enabled. |
| `assets/` indexes and objects | Optional: forces a re-download from Mojang. |
| Mod caches under `config/<mod>/` | Found automatically at any depth; only folders named `cache`. |

User data is never touched: `saves/`, `resourcepacks/`, `shaderpacks/`,
`screenshots/`, `mods/*.jar` and the top-level files in `config/` are excluded
by construction, and an empty target folder is left in place (the game expects
it to exist).

## Using it

- **Title screen** → `CleanMCMod...` button (top right).
- In game: **F7**.
- Command: `/cleanmcmod scan`, `/cleanmcmod clean`, `/cleanmcmod s [… 1,295 characters omitted] all**) and then confirm. The install step:

1. downloads to a temporary file,
2. verifies the SHA-1 Modrinth publishes,
3. moves the old jar aside, moves the new one in,
4. restores the old jar if anything fails.

There is no auto-update, no self-update, and no restart: new versions load the
next time you start the game. If a jar is locked by a running game the step
fails safely and says so.

Offline, unknown project, no matching version, unreadable jar, hash mismatch —
each leaves `mods/` exactly as it was and shows one readable message.

## Supported versions

Built for **Minecraft 1.21.8** by default. The Minecraft version is a build
dimension in `gradle.properties` (`minecraft_version`, `yarn_mappings`,
`fabric_api_version`, `java_version`); 1.21.9 / 1.21.10 / 1.21.11 use Java 21,
26.1 / 26.2 / 26.3 need Java 25. Only the 1.21.8 build has been compiled and
run; the other targets are untested.

Fabric Loader is the only loader. Quilt compatibility is unproven.

## Languages

`en_us` is canonical. Shipped translations: German, Spanish, French, Italian,
Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Turkish,
Ukrainian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese.

The reference project [PiBOH/vivi-music-de](https://github.com/PiBOH/vivi-music-de)
ships 47 language variants; the rest are still to be translated (see
`AGENTS.md` §6 for the list, the Minecraft code mapping and the parity check).

## Building from source

Java 25 is needed for Loom itself; the toolchain compiles to Java 21.

```bash
export JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-25
gradle clean build     # 50 unit tests + jar in build/libs/
gradle runClient       # dev client, game directory ./run
```

The version comes from `version.txt` (single source of truth); the artifact is
`cleanmcmod-<version>+<minecraft_version>.jar`.

## Not in this mod

- Hiding installed mods from servers, defeating mod/anti-cheat detection, or
  faking acceptance of a server resource pack. These are deliberate omissions:
  they break the Modrinth content rules and server terms of service.
- Anything server-side.
- Telemetry, analytics, background checks.

MIT. See `LICENSE` in the jar (added by the build) and in the repository.

version = "${modVersion}+${mcVersion}"
group = 'piboh.cleanmc.mod'

base {
    archivesName = 'cleanmcmod'
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    minecraft "com.mojang:minecraft:${mcVersion}"
    mappings "net.fabricmc:yarn:${yarnMappings}:v2"
    modImplementation "net.fabricmc:fabric-loader:${loader_version}"
    modImplementation "net.fabricmc.fabric-api:fabric-api:${fabricApiVersion}"

    testImplementation platform('org.junit:junit-bom:5.11.4')
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter'
    testImplementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.11.0'
    testRuntimeOnly 'org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher'
}

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(javaVersion)
    }
    withSourcesJar()
}

tasks.withType(JavaCompile).configureEach {
    options.encoding = 'UTF-8'
    options.release = javaVersion
}

processResources {
    inputs.property 'version', modVersion
    inputs.property 'minecraft_dep', mcDep
    filesMatching('fabric.mod.json') {
        expand version: modVersion, minecraft_dep: mcDep
    }
}

tasks.named('test') {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    testLogging {
        events 'passed', 'failed', 'skipped'
    }
}

jar {
    from(rootProject.file('LICENSE')) {
        rename { "${it}_cleanmcmod" }
    }
}

## Cosa ho consegnato, con numeri veri

Il versionamento è ora un parametro: `./gradlew clean build -Pmc=<versione>` legge una **matrice in [build.gradle](build.gradle)** con Yarn, Fabric API, livello Java e range `minecraft` per ogni riga. Senza `-Pmc` restano i default di [gradle.properties](gradle.properties) (1.21.8) — la build di default è identica a prima.

| Target | Comando | Esito | Jar | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.21.8 | `./gradlew clean build` | **BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 51s** | `cleanmcmod-0.1.0+1.21.8.jar` 123.526 B | 50/50 |
| 1.21.9 | `-Pmc=1.21.9` | **SUCCESSFUL in 14s** | `…+1.21.9.jar` 123.615 B | 50/50 |
| 1.21.10 | `-Pmc=1.21.10` | **SUCCESSFUL in 9s** | `…+1.21.10.jar` 123.612 B | 50/50 |
| 1.21.11 | `-Pmc=1.21.11` | **SUCCESSFUL in 12s** | `…+1.21.11.jar` 123.613 B | 50/50 |
| 26.1 / 26.2 / 26.3 | `-Pmc=26.1` | **BLOCCATO** al `:mappings` | — | — |

Ogni riga è stata compilata davvero, non copiata: la 1.21.9 ha richiesto modifiche al codice (sotto), la 1.21.10/1.21.11 hanno fatto scaricare i propri Yarn (`1.21.10+build.3`, `1.21.11+build.6`) e la propria Fabric API (`0.138.4+1.21.10`, `0.141.6+1.21.11`). Il jar 1.21.11 dichiara `0.1.0 / >=1.21.11 <1.21.12 / environment: client`.

## Perché 1.21.9 non compilava, e cosa ho toccato

Tre errori reali: `new KeyBinding(..., String category)` non esiste più (ora `KeyBinding.Category`), e `Screen.mouseClicked(double,double,int)` è diventato `mouseClicked(Click, boolean)`. Shim minimi, due file per API:

- **`AbstractUpdatesScreen`** (in `src/main/java`): tutto il corpo del vecchio `ModUpdatesScreen`, con l'hit-test estratto in `clickRow(x, y, button)`.
- **`src/compat/1.21.8/java/.../ModUpdatesScreen.java`** (13 righe): override con la vecchia firma; **`src/compat/1.21.9/java/.../ModUpdatesScreen.java`** (18 righe): override con `Click`.
- **`MenuKey`** nei due stessi dir: stringa `"key.categories.cleanmcmod"` sulla 1.21.8, `KeyBinding.Category.MISC` sulla 1.21.9+ — MISC per non inventare una chiave di traduzione che i file lang non hanno (non li ho toccati).

`build.gradle` sceglie la cartella compat in base a `-Pmc`. Nessuna duplicazione dello schermo da 236 righe.

Verifica a livello di bytecode, non solo "compila": nel jar **1.21.8** `ModUpdatesScreen` espone `method_25402(double, double, int)` e il `MenuKey` carica la costante `"key.categories.cleanmcmod"`; nel jar **1.21.11** lo stesso metodo è `method_25402(class_11909, boolean)` e `MenuKey` usa `Category`. Entrambi delegano a `AbstractUpdatesScreen.clickRow`.

## 26.x: dove si ferma, esattamente

1. **`:mappings`** — `Could not find net.fabricmc:yarn:26.1+build.1`; su `maven.fabricmc.net` l'ultima Yarn pubblicata è `1.21.11+build.6`, zero versioni `26.x` (verificato sull'elenco completo, 3412 build).
2. Con **Mojang mappings**: `Failed to find official mojang mappings for 26.1`.
3. Senza mappings: Loom 1.19.3 rifiuta (`Configuration 'mappings' has no dependencies`). Il `build.gradle` ufficiale di Fabric per la 26.3 usa **`loom_version=1.19-SNAPSHOT`**, nessuna riga `mappings` e `implementation` invece di `modImplementation`: la 26.x è **deobfuscata**.
4. Con `1.19-SNAPSHOT` la 26.1 arriva più avanti ma muore su `fabric-api`: `Expected official namespace for access widener entry, found: intermediary in mod: fabric-biome-api-v1`.

Quindi la 26.x non è uno shim: serve un'altra linea di Loom (SNAPSHOT, non pinnabile per una CI), nessuna mappatura, e rinominare ogni classe Minecraft-facing. **Non ho creato workflow per 26.x** — sarebbero rossi al primo push.

## CI

Quattro file, uno per versione: [build-1.21.8.yml](.github/workflows/build-1.21.8.yml), [build-1.21.9.yml](.github/workflows/build-1.21.9.yml), [build-1.21.10.yml](.github/workflows/build-1.21.10.yml), [build-1.21.11.yml](.github/workflows/build-1.21.11.yml), ognuno con JDK 21 (toolchain) + JDK 25 (Loom), wrapper-validation, e `-Pmc=<versione>`. Ho rimosso `build.yml`, che avrebbe duplicato la 1.21.8. Tutti e quattro parsano con SnakeYAML e il comando espanso è corretto. Ho aggiornato solo la lista versioni in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [README.md](README.md) e `gradle.properties`.

## Cosa NON ho verificato

Il click sulle righe della schermata Aggiornamenti **non l'ho cliccato** in questa tornata: la modifica è provata da compilazione, bytecode e dai 50 test di logica, non da un client avviato — né su 1.21.8 (regressione visiva) né su 1.21.9+, che non ho mai lanciato. Nessun commit: la cartella non è un repository git, come da istruzioni.

package piboh.cleanmc.mod.update;

/**
 * The small subset of Fabric's version predicates that mods actually declare in
 * {@code fabric.mod.json}: {@code >=1.0 <2.0}, {@code <2.0.0}, {@code =1.2}, {@code ~1.2.3},
 * {@code ^1.2.3}, {@code 1.2.x} and {@code *}.
 */
public final class VersionRange {

    private VersionRange() {
    }

    /** @return true/false when the predicate can be evaluated, {@code null} when it cannot */
    public static Boolean satisfies(String version, String predicate) {
        if (predicate == null || predicate.isBlank()) {
            return null;
        }
        for (String token : predicate.trim().split("\\s+")) {
            Boolean one = single(version, token);
            if (one == null || !one) {
                return one;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    private static Boolean single(String version, String token) {
        if (token.equals("*") || token.equalsIgnoreCase("x")) {
            return true;
        }
        String prefix = operator(token);
        String bound = token.substring(prefix.length()).trim();
        if (bound.isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }
        if (bound.equalsIgnoreCase("x") || bound.endsWith(".x") || bound.endsWith(".X")) {
            String base = bound.substring(0, bound.length() - 1);
            return prefix.isEmpty() || prefix.equals("=")
                    ? startsWithSegment(version, base)
                    : null;
        }
        if (!bound.matches("[0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*")) {
            return null;
        }
        return switch (prefix) {
            case ">=" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) >= 0;
            case ">" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) > 0;
            case "<=" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) <= 0;
            case "<" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) < 0;
            case "=", "" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) == 0;
            case "~" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) >= 0
                    && VersionComparator.compare(version, bump(bound, 1)) < 0;
            case "^" -> VersionComparator.compare(version, bound) >= 0
                    && VersionComparator.compare(version, bump(bound, 0)) < 0;
            default -> null;
        };
    }

    private static String operator(String token) {
        for (String candidate : new String[] {">=", "<=", ">", "<", "=", "~", "^"}) {
            if (token.startsWith(candidate)) {
                return candidate;
            }
        }
        return "";
    }

    /** {@code 1} bumps the minor, {@code 0} the major: {@code 1.2.3} becomes {@code 1.3.0} / {@code 2.0.0}. */
    private static String bump(String version, int index) {
        String[] parts = version.split("\\.");
        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(parts.length, index + 1); i++) {
            if (i > 0) {
                out.append('.');
            }
            if (i < index) {
                out.append(parts[i]);
            } else if (i == index) {
                out.append(number(parts[i]) + 1);
            } else {
                out.append('0');
            }
        }
        return out.toString();
    }

    private static boolean startsWithSegment(String version, String base) {
        return version.startsWith(base) && (version.length() == base.length()
                || !Character.isDigit(version.charAt(base.length())));
    }

    private static int number(String part) {
        StringBuilder digits = new StringBuilder();
        for (char c : part.toCharArray()) {
            if (!Character.isDigit(c)) {
                break;
            }
            digits.append(c);
        }
        return digits.length() == 0 ? 0 : Integer.parseInt(digits.toString());
    }
}

package piboh.cleanmc.mod.update;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * The pre-flight a mod update has to pass before it may touch {@code mods/}.
 *
 * <p>Pure: it reads the candidate's Modrinth dependencies, the jars that are actually installed and
 * the requirements those jars declare in their own {@code fabric.mod.json}, and answers
 * install / warn / block with a reason a player can read.</p>
 */
public final class Compatibility {

    /** Ids the loader or the game provides, so they are never a missing jar. */
    private static final Set<String> PLATFORM_IDS = Set.of(
            "fabric-api", "fabricloader", "minecraft", "java", "quilt_loader", "quilted_fabric_api");

    public enum Status {
        OK,
        WARN,
        BLOCK
    }

    /** @param reason null when there is nothing to say */
    public record Verdict(Status status, String reason) {

        public static final Verdict OK = new Verdict(Status.OK, null);

        public static Verdict block(String reason) {
            return new Verdict(Status.BLOCK, reason);
        }

        public static Verdict warn(String reason) {
            return new Verdict(Status.WARN, reason);
        }

        public boolean blocks() {
            return status == Status.BLOCK;
        }
    }

    private Compatibility() {
    }

    /**
     * @param updated            the installed jar that would be replaced
     * @param candidate          the version that would replace it
     * @param installed          every jar in {@code mods/}, the updated one included
     * @param projectIdByModId   Modrinth project id of each installed mod, when known
     * @param titles             project id to display name, from Modrinth
     */
    public static Verdict check(
            LocalMod updated,
            ModVersion candidate,
            List<LocalMod> installed,
            Map<String, String> projectIdByModId,
            Map<String, String> titles) {

        for (Dependency dependency : candidate.dependencies()) {
            if (dependency.incompatible() && projectIdByModId.containsValue(dependency.projectId())) {
                return Verdict.block("it is incompatible with " + name(dependency.projectId(), titles)
                        + ", which is installed");
            }
        }

        for (Dependency dependency : candidate.dependencies()) {
            if (!dependency.required()) {
                continue;
            }
            if (projectIdByModId.containsValue(dependency.projectId())) {
                continue;
            }
            if (PLATFORM_IDS.contains(dependency.projectId())) {
                continue;
            }
            return Verdict.block("it needs " + name(dependency.projectId(), titles)
                    + ", which is not in mods/ — install that first");
        }

        for (LocalMod other : installed) {
            if (other.modId() == null || other.modId().equals(updated.modId())) {
                continue;
            }
            String range = other.depends().get(updated.modId());
            if (range == null) {
                continue;
            }
            Boolean satisfied = VersionRange.satisfies(candidate.versionNumber(), range);
            if (satisfied == null) {
                return Verdict.warn(other.modId() + " asks for " + updated.modId() + " " + range
                        + ", which cannot be checked");
            }
            if (!satisfied) {
                return Verdict.block(other.modId() + " needs " + updated.modId() + " " + range
                        + ", so " + candidate.versionNumber() + " would break it");
            }
        }
        return Verdict.OK;
    }

    private static String name(String projectId, Map<String, String> titles) {
        String title = titles == null ? null : titles.get(projectId);
        return title == null || title.isBlank() ? projectId : title;
    }
}

package piboh.cleanmc.mod.update;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;

/** The dependency pre-flight, checked against payloads captured from the Modrinth API. */
class CompatibilityTest {

    /** Captured 2026-10-25 from /v2/project/iris/version?game_versions=["1.21.8"]&loaders=["fabric"]. */
    private static final String IRIS_VERSION = """
            {
              "id": "Rhzf61g1",
              "project_id": "YL57xq9U",
              "version_number": "1.9.6+1.21.8-fabric",
              "game_versions": ["1.21.6", "1.21.7", "1.21.8"],
              "loaders": ["fabric"],
              "dependencies": [
                {
                  "version_id": "pJRT8Zxt",
                  "project_id": "AANobbMI",
                  "file_name": null,
                  "dependency_type": "required"
                }
              ],
              "files": [
                {
                  "primary": true,
                  "filename": "iris-fabric-1.9.6+mc1.21.8.jar",
                  "url": "https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/YL57xq9U/versions/Rhzf61g1/iris-fabric-1.9.6%2Bmc1.21.8.jar",
                  "hashes": {"sha1": "70fc97aa5eef2df2085a078ecb17d6bfce6756dd"}
                }
              ]
            }
            """;

    private static final String SODIUM_PROJECT = "AANobbMI";
    private static final String FABRIC_API_PROJECT = "P7dR8mSH";
    private static final Map<String, String> TITLES =
            Map.of(SODIUM_PROJECT, "Sodium", "YL57xq9U", "Iris Shaders");

    private static ModVersion iris() {
        Map<String, ModVersion> parsed = ModrinthClient.parseVersions(
                "{\"70fc97aa5eef2df2085a078ecb17d6bfce6756dd\": " + IRIS_VERSION + "}");
        return parsed.get("70fc97aa5eef2df2085a078ecb17d6bfce6756dd");
    }

    private static LocalMod jar(String modId, String version, Map<String, String> depends) {
        return new LocalMod(Path.of("/tmp/mods/" + modId + ".jar"), "sha-" + modId, modId, version, depends);
    }

    @Test
    void readsRequiredDependencyFromCapturedPayload() {
        assertTrue(iris().dependencies().contains(new Dependency(SODIUM_PROJECT, "pJRT8Zxt", "required")));
    }

    @Test
    void blocksWhenRequiredDependencyIsNotInstalled() {
        LocalMod irisJar = jar("iris", "1.9.5+1.21.8-fabric", Map.of());
        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(irisJar, iris(), List.of(irisJar),
                Map.of("iris", "YL57xq9U"), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.BLOCK, verdict.status());
        assertTrue(verdict.reason().contains("Sodium"), verdict.reason());
        assertTrue(verdict.reason().contains("not in mods/"), verdict.reason());
    }

    @Test
    void allowsInstallingWhenRequiredDependencyIsPresent() {
        LocalMod irisJar = jar("iris", "1.9.5+1.21.8-fabric", Map.of());
        LocalMod sodiumJar = jar("sodium", "0.6.5+mc1.21.8", Map.of());

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(irisJar, iris(), List.of(irisJar, sodiumJar),
                Map.of("iris", "YL57xq9U", "sodium", SODIUM_PROJECT), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.OK, verdict.status());
        assertFalse(verdict.blocks());
    }

    @Test
    void doesNotCountLoaderProvidedDependenciesAsMissing() {
        ModVersion candidate = new ModVersion("v1", "YL57xq9U", "1.9.6", "iris.jar", "https://example.invalid",
                "sha", List.of("1.21.8"), List.of("fabric"),
                List.of(new Dependency(FABRIC_API_PROJECT, null, "required")));
        LocalMod irisJar = jar("iris", "1.9.5", Map.of());

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(irisJar, candidate, List.of(irisJar),
                Map.of("iris", "YL57xq9U"), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.OK, verdict.status());
    }

    @Test
    void blocksWhenAnotherModsVersionRangeWouldBreak() {
        LocalMod sodiumJar = jar("sodium", "0.6.5+mc1.21.8", Map.of());
        LocalMod extraJar = jar("sodium-extra", "0.6.0", Map.of("sodium", ">=0.6.0 <0.7.0"));
        ModVersion candidate = new ModVersion("v2", SODIUM_PROJECT, "0.7.0+mc1.21.8", "sodium.jar",
                "https://example.invalid", "sha", List.of("1.21.8"), List.of("fabric"));

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(sodiumJar, candidate, List.of(sodiumJar, extraJar),
                Map.of("sodium", SODIUM_PROJECT), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.BLOCK, verdict.status());
        assertTrue(verdict.reason().contains("sodium-extra"), verdict.reason());
        assertTrue(verdict.reason().contains("0.7.0"), verdict.reason());
    }

    @Test
    void allowsAnUpdateInsideTheDeclaredRange() {
        LocalMod sodiumJar = jar("sodium", "0.6.5+mc1.21.8", Map.of());
        LocalMod extraJar = jar("sodium-extra", "0.6.0", Map.of("sodium", ">=0.6.0 <0.7.0"));
        ModVersion candidate = new ModVersion("v3", SODIUM_PROJECT, "0.6.9", "sodium.jar",
                "https://example.invalid", "sha", List.of("1.21.8"), List.of("fabric"));

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(sodiumJar, candidate, List.of(sodiumJar, extraJar),
                Map.of("sodium", SODIUM_PROJECT), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.OK, verdict.status());
    }

    @Test
    void blocksIncompatiblePair() {
        LocalMod sodiumJar = jar("sodium", "0.6.5", Map.of());
        LocalMod updatedJar = jar("some-renderer", "1.0", Map.of());
        ModVersion candidate = new ModVersion("v4", "SOMERENDERER", "2.0", "renderer.jar",
                "https://example.invalid", "sha", List.of("1.21.8"), List.of("fabric"),
                List.of(new Dependency(SODIUM_PROJECT, null, "incompatible")));

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(updatedJar, candidate,
                List.of(updatedJar, sodiumJar), Map.of("sodium", SODIUM_PROJECT), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.BLOCK, verdict.status());
        assertTrue(verdict.reason().contains("incompatible"), verdict.reason());
    }

    @Test
    void warnsWhenAnotherModsRangeCannotBeRead() {
        LocalMod sodiumJar = jar("sodium", "0.6.5", Map.of());
        LocalMod otherJar = jar("other", "1.0", Map.of("sodium", "weird-syntax"));
        ModVersion candidate = new ModVersion("v5", SODIUM_PROJECT, "0.7.0", "sodium.jar",
                "https://example.invalid", "sha", List.of("1.21.8"), List.of("fabric"));

        Compatibility.Verdict verdict = Compatibility.check(sodiumJar, candidate,
                List.of(sodiumJar, otherJar), Map.of("sodium", SODIUM_PROJECT), TITLES);

        assertEquals(Compatibility.Status.WARN, verdict.status());
        assertFalse(verdict.blocks());
    }

    @Test
    void readsTheVersionPredicatesModsActuallyUse() {
        assertEquals(Boolean.TRUE, VersionRange.satisfies("0.6.5", ">=0.6.0 <0.7.0"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.FALSE, VersionRange.satisfies("0.7.0", ">=0.6.0 <0.7.0"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.TRUE, VersionRange.satisfies("1.2.9", "~1.2.3"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.FALSE, VersionRange.satisfies("1.3.0", "~1.2.3"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.TRUE, VersionRange.satisfies("1.9.6", "^1.2.3"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.TRUE, VersionRange.satisfies("0.136.1", "0.136.x"));
        assertEquals(Boolean.TRUE, VersionRange.satisfies("9.9.9", "*"));
        assertEquals(null, VersionRange.satisfies("1.0", "weird-syntax"));
    }
}

## Cosa ho aggiunto

Il pre-flight vive in classi pure accanto alla decisione esistente, non dentro schermo o installer:

| File | Ruolo |
|---|---|
| [Compatibility.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/Compatibility.java) | `check(updated, candidate, installed, projectIdByModId, titles)` → `Verdict(OK/WARN/BLOCK, reason)` |
| [VersionRange.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/VersionRange.java) | i predicati che le mod dichiarano davvero: `>=1.0 <2.0`, `~1.2.3`, `^1.2.3`, `1.2.x`, `*`, `=` |
| [Dependency.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/Dependency.java) | una voce di `dependencies` di Modrinth (`required`/`incompatible`/…) |

Il resto sono ritocchi mirati: `ModVersion` porta le dipendenze, `ModrinthClient` le parsa e chiede a Modrinth anche i **titoli** dei progetti dipendenti (così il motivo dice "Sodium", non `AANobbMI`); `ModScanner` legge il blocco `depends` dal `fabric.mod.json` di ogni jar; `ModUpdate` porta il verdetto; `ModUpdaterService.installAsync` salta gli update bloccati registrando il motivo come esito; la lista mostra la riga bloccata con **⚠ e colore d'errore** già prima del click.

Regole, in ordine:

1. **BLOCK** — una dipendenza `required` non è installata (e non è Fabric API, che il launcher fornisce);
2. **BLOCK** — una dipendenza `incompatible` corrisponde a un progetto installato;
3. **BLOCK** — un'altra mod installata dichiara un range su questa e la nuova versione lo viola (`sodium-extra needs sodium >=0.6.0 <0.7.0, so 0.7.0 would break it`);
4. **WARN** — il range di un'altra mod non è interpretabile (`cannot be checked`);
5. **OK** — altrimenti l'installazione procede come prima.

Nessuna chiave di traduzione nuova (i motivi sono testo costruito): i 15 file lang restano a parità.

## Prove

**JUnit — 60 test, 0 fallimenti** (10 nuovi): `CompatibilityTest` (8: payload reale di Iris parsato, dipendenza mancante, dipendenza soddisfatta, Fabric API non bloccante, violazione di range, update dentro il range, coppia incompatibile, range illeggibile) + `readsTheVersionPredicatesModsActuallyUse`, e `ModUpdaterServiceTest.blockedUpdateIsReportedAndNeverDownloaded` che verifica che il downloader **non venga mai chiamato** e che il vecchio jar resti.

**Contro l'API vera**, harness headless sulle classi compilate con hashes reali (poi cancellato):

```
== only iris installed ==
  Iris Shaders 1.9.5+1.21.8-fabric -> 1.9.6+1.21.8-fabric | BLOCK | blocked=true
  | it needs Sodium, which is not in mods/ — install that first
== iris + sodium installed ==
  Iris Shaders 1.9.5+1.21.8-fabric -> 1.9.6+1.21.8-fabric | OK | blocked=false
```

| Target | Esito | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1.21.8 | BUILD SUCCESSFUL 11s (finale: 8s) | 60/60 |
| 1.21.9 | SUCCESSFUL 8s | 60/60 |
| 1.21.10 | SUCCESSFUL 8s | 60/60 |
| 1.21.11 | SUCCESSFUL 10s | 60/60 |

## Limiti, detti chiaro

- Il caso "incompatibile" non ha un payload **catturato**: nessuna delle mod che ho interrogato (sodium, iris, lithium, nvidium, vulkanmod, distant-horizons…) pubblica dipendenze `incompatible`; il test usa la stessa forma esatta dello schema Modrinth, non una riga scaricata.
- Il pre-flight **blocca ma non installa** la dipendenza mancante: la missione diceva "aggiorna se può", e questa mod non scarica dipendenze da sola.
- Falso blocco possibile: una dipendenza è considerata presente solo se il suo progetto è noto a Modrinth tramite `/version_files`; una mod installata che Modrinth non conosce (build di sviluppo, CurseForge-only) non conta.
- Non ho visto il verdetto **dentro il client**: il comportamento è provato da test e dall'harness, non da uno screenshot della lista con la riga ⚠.
- Niente commit: `M README.md` e i file nuovi restano non committati, come chiesto.

## Cosa è cambiato

Due difetti, entrambi introdotti dal passaggio precedente, chiusi con lo stesso dato: il verdetto.

**1. La dipendenza installata viene ora confrontata per build, non per presenza.** Iris 1.9.6 pinna Sodium a `pJRT8Zxt` (0.7.2); un Sodium 0.7.0 installato passava la verifica perché il progetto c'era. Ora [Compatibility.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/Compatibility.java) confronta l'id Modrinth della build installata (dallo SHA-1 che il check già calcola) con il `version_id` che il candidato pinna, e in caso di mismatch blocca *con piano*: `missing` = progetto, `outdated` = mappa progetto→jar da sostituire.

Perché per id e non per stringa di versione — l'ho verificato sull'API vera: Sodium ha cambiato schema a metà storia (`0.5.8+mc1.20.1` → `mc1.21.8-0.7.2-fabric`). Qualsiasi ordinamento tra stringhe dei due schemi risponde il contrario del vero. L'id Modrinth è esatto; il confronto tra pari-schema sarebbe una scommessa.

**2. La riga ora dice quello che il servizio farà davvero.** `ModUpdate.resolvable()` ([ModUpdate.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/ModUpdate.java)) è l'unica regola, usata sia dal servizio sia dallo schermo:

| Verdetto | Marcatore | Colore | Al click |
|---|---|---|---|
| OK | `▸` se selezionata | verde | aggiorna |
| BLOCK con dipendenza risolvibile (`＋`) | `＋` | ambra | scarica dipendenza + update |
| BLOCK non risolvibile (`⚠`) | `⚠` | rosso | rifiutato, motivo in esito |
| WARN | nessuno | bianco | aggiorna, motivo in tooltip |

Il motivo compare **prima** del click: hover sulla riga → tooltip ([AbstractUpdatesScreen.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/ui/AbstractUpdatesScreen.java)), una riga ritagliata a 220px, nessuna chiave nuova. Anche i WARN hanno qualcosa da dire.

## Difetti trovati attaccando il codice (e corretti)

1. **Cancellare una dipendenza già aggiornata.** Se il piano risolve una dipendenza alla build *già installata*, il download viene saltato — ma il jar "vecchio" era comunque nella lista da ritirare: sarebbe stato cancellato, lasciando il gioco senza Sodium. Ora si ritira solo ciò che il batch ha davvero scaricato (`retireReplaced`).
2. **Re-upload con lo stesso nome file.** Se la build nuova si chiama come la vecchia, il move la scrive e il retire la cancellava subito dopo. Guardia sul nome + test dedicato.
3. **Doppio download.** Una mod e la sua dipendenza possono essere entrambe nella lista update: lo stesso jar veniva scaricato due volte. Dedupe per SHA-1 in [ModInstaller.java](src/main/java/piboh/cleanmc/mod/update/ModInstaller.java).

## Prove

**JUnit 73 test, 0 fallimenti** (7 nuovi): build diversa da quella pinnata → BLOCK con `outdated`; build esattamente pinnata → OK; jar sconosciuto a Modrinth → solo presenza (niente blocchi inventati); dipendenza obsoleta sostituita e vecchio jar rimosso; dipendenza già alla build risolta → non scaricata e **non** cancellata; sostituzione con lo stesso nome file → il jar nuovo sopravvive; marcatura della riga per OK/risolvibile/bloccato/warn.

**API vera, tre scenari** (harness headless sulle classi compilate, poi cancellato):

```
# iris 1.9.5 + sodium 0.7.0 installati
check: Iris Shaders 1.9.5+mc1.21.8 -> 1.9.6+1.21.8-fabric | blocked=true resolvable=true
       missing=[AANobbMI] outdated=[AANobbMI]
       | it asks for a different Sodium build than the installed mc1.21.8-0.7.0-fabric
install: Iris success=true / Sodium success=true
mods/: iris-fabric-1.9.6+mc1.21.8.jar, sodium-fabric-0.7.3+mc1.21.8.jar   ← un solo Sodium
recheck updates=0
```

```
# iris 1.9.5 + sodium 0.7.3 (più nuova della build pinnata)
check: blocked=true resolvable=true | it asks for a different Sodium build than the installed mc1.21.8-0.7.3-fabric
install: Iris success=true
mods/: iris-fabric-1.9.6+mc1.21.8.jar, sodium-0.7.3.jar   ← NON cancellato
```

```

old update jar kept=true  new jar absent=true  unresolved dependency jar kept=true
```

**Build, tutti verdi, 73 test su ognuno:** 1.21.8 (11s), 1.21.9 (10s), 1.21.10 (8s), 1.21.11 (8s). Parità lang: 15 file, 79 chiavi, nessuna chiave nuova. Nessun commit: resta solo `Initial commit`, tutto il resto non committato.

## Limiti, detti chiari

- **La metà UI non è vista dentro il gioco**: `＋`/`⚠` e il tooltip sono provati dal test sulla regola condivisa e dalla compilazione sui quattro target, non da uno screenshot in Minecraft. Non ho avviato il client in questo passaggio.
- Un jar che Modrinth non conosce (build di sviluppo, CurseForge-only) resta verificato solo per presenza: non c'è modo di sapere che build sia.
- Una dipendenza **più nuova** della build pinnata viene comunque marcata `＋`: il piano risolve alla latest, che è quella già installata, quindi non scarica né cancella nulla (scenario 2), ma il motivo dice "asks for a different build" anche quando va tutto bene.
- 26.1/26.2/26.3 e i branch per versione restano assenti; le lingue sono 15 su 47.

Ho saltato: verifica in-game, branch per versione, 26.x, resto delle lingue. Rischio residuo: il tooltip è una riga sola — un motivo lunghissimo viene troncato a 220px.
